surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground, flat terrain tiles seen from above

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tileset sheet: grey asphalt road shapes (crossroads, dead ends, 1-wide and 3-wide straight runs) laid on a brown dirt ground that fills the full 368-wide by 304-row silhouette. It is drawn flat from above, with no standing volume. The dark brown ledge on the south side is a thin edge strip (about 1-2 rows) and does not form a front face of 3 or more rows. Column scans show only alternating mottling and dirt bands, with no top band ending in a front-edge line and no eave shadow. As flat ground terrain it has no front face, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt patches show about 4 grey steps, with a lighter worn mottling on the sides and thin brown cracks. Large interior areas of the dark charcoal are one flat colour with no dot or grain. The measured near-flat coverage is 24%, against 0% for both references. Visible tones per tile are 5, above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). The edges are tinted brown (0% neutral), so they read as dark material tone. The dirt surround is well textured, but the road itself, which is the subject, is flatter and sparser than the references. The mottling is chunky, with few aggregate pixels. A careful artist would see the large flat charcoal blocks as thinner than the reference.
